cards.title: PEBELS: Policy Exposure Based Excess Loss Smoothing
cards.claim: Rare, very large non-catastrophe property losses make up a disproportionate share of property loss, and empirical excess-loss factors are volatile and non-credible for small segments of a book.
cards.relevance: Supports treating 88 large claims as important while warning that a small insurer's own excess-loss ratios are too volatile to price directly.
cards.limit: US commercial property focus; proposes a method rather than reporting a concentration percentage.

cards.title: Multi-bureau study of mega claims in workers' compensation
cards.publisher: Insurance Journal (reporting WCIRB and nine other rating bureaus)
cards.claim: Claims above a $2 million threshold are a tiny fraction of claims yet account for a small but material slice of total loss dollars.

stat.what: Workers' comp claims above $2M incurred, accident years 2001-2021

cards.relevance: Shows how concentration depends on threshold choice; a $10K threshold capturing 10% of claims and 32% of dollars is far less extreme than mega-claim tails.
cards.limit: Workers' compensation, not Canadian home or auto, and a much higher threshold.

cards.title: 2024 shatters record for costliest year for severe weather-related losses
cards.claim: IBC reports 2024 insured severe-weather losses of about $8.5 billion, and says personal property claims and repair or replacement costs have both risen sharply since 2019.

stat.what: Personal property damage, as stated by IBC

cards.relevance: Frames cat-driven severity and repair-cost escalation behind rising average claim size.
cards.limit: Industry advocacy release; the 485% basis is not defined on the page and is catastrophe-skewed.

cards.title: Insurance in Canada: What's driving premiums higher?
cards.claim: Residential construction prices rose far faster than homeowners' maintenance and repair costs between late 2019 and late 2025, while homeowner insurance expenses hit a record in 2024.
cards.relevance: Supports inflation of rebuild cost as a driver of large property claims, while showing smaller repair items rose less.

cards.title: Inflationary pressures continue to create challenges for property insurance market
cards.claim: IBC cites Statistics Canada data showing residential building costs and key materials rose much faster than general inflation over five years.

stat.what: Residential construction costs vs general inflation, five years (Feb 2025)

cards.relevance: Quantifies materials and construction inflation that lifts severity of fire and water claims.
cards.limit: Advocacy piece; labour cost figures not given; period differs from SC-04.

cards.title: Huntsville fire highlights gaps in coverage, rising property claims
cards.claim: Trade press reports average residential fire claim payouts rose over the past two years, attributed to inflation and total-loss events.

stat.what: Increase in average residential fire payout over two years (Oct 2025)

cards.relevance: Consistent with fire being rare but severe, with severity trending upward.
cards.limit: Trade article, unnamed underlying source, no dollar average.

cards.title: Fire incidents increase during the pandemic
cards.claim: Residential fires are numerous but roughly 1% are fatal, and cooking is the leading cause of incidents.

stat.what: Reported residential fires across seven reporting jurisdictions

cards.relevance: Gives frequency context for fire as a low-frequency peril; official source for Canadian fire counts.
cards.limit: No dollar-loss or insured-claim data on the page.

cards.title: Flooding insurance Ontario (Rates.ca Home Insuramap report)
cards.claim: Rates.ca estimates basement water repair costs at least $43,000 out of pocket, and a single water claim lifts Ontario premiums noticeably.

stat.what: Estimated basement repair cost; premium rise about $376/yr (19%)

cards.relevance: Indicates a single water loss can exceed the $10,000 large-claim threshold, consistent with 41 of 88 large claims being water.
cards.limit: Quote-based estimate from a comparison site, not paid-claim averages.

cards.title: Rising water damage claims push home insurance costs higher
cards.claim: Basement water-damage repair costs rose about 20% from 2019 to 2024, with flooding contributing over $1 billion in 2024 damages.

stat.what: Rise in basement water repair cost, 2019-2024

cards.relevance: Shows water severity rising moderately, relevant to water being the largest share of large claims.
cards.limit: Insurer-sourced trade report; no average claim dollar figure.

cards.title: Excess of loss reinsurance
cards.claim: Per-risk excess-of-loss cover reimburses an insurer for single-risk losses above a retention, separate from catastrophe cover that responds to multi-policy events.
cards.relevance: Explains the structure that would cap net retained cost of rare severe fire losses.
cards.limit: Educational primer with commercial-scale example; retentions for a personal-lines book would be far smaller; year approximate.

cards.title: 4 Reasons for Reserve Deficiencies That No One Talks About
cards.claim: Practitioners recommend a cross-functional large loss committee and investigating reserve changes of ten percent or more on a claim.

stat.what: Reserve adjustment size that should prompt investigation

cards.relevance: Offers a concrete senior-claim review practice for the 88 large claims.
cards.limit: Practitioner opinion, US, nearly ten years old.

cards.title: Litigation costs drive US liability claims by 57% over past decade: Swiss Re Institute
cards.claim: Swiss Re attributes a large rise in US liability claims to social inflation and estimates a roughly 7% effect in Canada in 2023 tied to mass torts.

stat.what: Social inflation impact on liability claims

cards.relevance: Explains why 17 liability claims could be in the large-claim tail.
cards.limit: Mostly US evidence; Canadian figure is a secondary-source estimate for commercial liability, not personal-lines liability.

cards.title: Social inflation reached 20-year high of 7 percent in 2023
cards.publisher: Construction Law / CLM Magazine (Swiss Re sigma)
cards.claim: Social inflation ran above economic inflation, with large verdicts multiplying and liability lines posting combined ratios above 100%.

stat.what: Average annual social vs economic inflation, 2017-2022

cards.relevance: Quantifies severity drift in liability beyond ordinary inflation.
cards.limit: US commercial liability; weak transfer to Canadian personal liability.

cards.title: Intact Q3 profit falls as storms hit home cover
cards.claim: Catastrophe losses, not individual large claims, were the main swing factor in a leading Canadian insurer's personal property results this quarter.

stat.what: Catastrophe contribution to personal property combined ratio of 105.0%, Q3 2026

cards.relevance: Cautions that portfolio volatility is driven largely by catastrophe events, so attritional large-claim review should not be conflated with cat exposure.
cards.limit: One insurer, one quarter, net of reinsurance; does not separate non-cat large losses.
